title: Man Jailed for Facebook Meme About Charlie Kirk Wins $835,000!
summary: Can you get arrested for a joke on social media? Larry Bushart found out the hard way — and now he's won a big settlement! The 61-year-old retired police officer from Tennessee posted a Facebook meme about Charlie Kirk, a conservative commentator. The meme showed President Trump and a quote he said after a school shooting: "We have to get over it." Bushart added, "This seems relevant today..." Some people in his town thought he was threatening a local school, even though the meme was about a school in Iowa. The sheriff arrested him for a felony, and Bushart spent 37 days in jail. He missed his wedding anniversary and the birth of his granddaughter. He also lost his job. But in October, the charge was dropped. Bushart then sued the county, the sheriff, and the investigator, saying his First Amendment right to free speech was violated. On Wednesday, he agreed to a settlement of $835,000. "I am pleased my First Amendment rights have been vindicated," Bushart said. His lawyers said the case shows that the government must respect free speech, especially when people are upset. "When government officials fail that test, the Constitution exists to hold them accountable," said attorney Cary Davis. So, what do you think? Should there be limits on what we can say online, even as a joke? This case reminds us that free speech can be messy — but it's a right we all have.
why_it_matters: This case shows that even a meme can land someone in jail, which could affect how you think about posting jokes and talking about serious topics online.

background_read: The First Amendment is a key part of the U.S. Constitution that protects people's right to say what they think, even if others disagree.
Charlie Kirk (a conservative commentator and founder of Turning Point USA) often talks about free speech and politics.
Sometimes, online jokes can be mistaken as real threats, which is why this case became a big fight over what 'free speech' means.

WHERE: The arrest happened in Tennessee, USA, and the court case took place there.
WHY: Bushart sued because he believed his arrest violated his First Amendment right to free speech, and the government paid to settle the case.
